answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a staking ladder. Each new identity must lock a refundable deposit in a shared lagoon pool, and only a long horizon of honest transactions unlocks higher trade limits. Newcomers start on a small knoll: they can trade tiny amounts, but large deals need endorsements from established agents who forfeit part of their own stake if the newcomer cheats. Spawning a thousand fakes means locking a thousand deposits and waiting out the horizon for each, while one honest agent pays once. Sybils become expensive and slow; honest entry stays cheap.
